title: The locus circle
subject: Pure Mathematics
summary: In the complex plane, |z − w| is a distance. A locus is every point that obeys a rule, so rules about distances draw circles. These notes cover reading a centre, avoiding sign traps, and completing the square.

notes.title: Distance and the circle
notes.text: |z − w| is the distance from the point z to the point w. So |z − w| = r describes every point at distance r from w: a circle with centre w and radius r. Example: |z − ({a} {b|s}i)| = {r} has centre ({a}, {b}) and radius {r}.
notes.hint: Read w straight from the bracket: z − w, so w is whatever is being subtracted.

why: The centre is the number being subtracted, {c} {d|s}i, so the point ({c}, {d}).
The signs are flipped. The centre is what is subtracted, unchanged.
x and y are swapped: the real part gives x.
Only the imaginary part has the wrong sign.

notes.title: Watch the signs
notes.text: Inside the modulus the signs flip: z + p − qi = z − (−p + qi), so the centre is (−p, q). Example: |z + {p1} − {q1}i| = {r1} has centre ({-p1}, {q1}).
notes.hint: Rewrite as z − (something) first. Then read the centre.

fb.{p},{-q}: The signs are the wrong way round: z + {p} − {q}i = z − (−{p} + {q}i).
fb.{p},{q}: z + {p} means the centre’s real part is −{p}, not {p}.

tasks.ex: z + {p} − {q}i = z − (−{p} + {q}i), so the centre is (−{p}, {q}).

notes.title: Complete the square
notes.text: Write z = x + yi. A circle x² + y² + 2px + 2qy + c = 0 has centre (−p, −q) and r² = p² + q² − c. Example: x² + y² {2*P1|s}x {2*Q1|s}y {C1|s} = 0 becomes (x {P1|s})² + (y {Q1|s})² = {P1*P1+Q1*Q1-C1}.
notes.hint: Halve the coefficients of x and y to get p and q. The centre is (−p, −q).

fb.{P},{Q},{R}: The centre is (−p, −q): change both signs.

tasks.ex: p = {P}, q = {Q}, so the centre is ({-P}, {-Q}) and r² = {P*P} + {Q*Q} − ({C}) = {R}.

notes.title: Spot the circle
notes.text: A rule like |z − p| = k|z − q| with k ≠ 1: square both sides and expand. The x² and y² terms then have the same coefficient, the sign of a circle. If k = 1 the squares cancel and you get a straight line instead.
notes.hint: A circle needs equal coefficients on x² and y², and no xy term.

tasks.q: Which of these equations describes a circle?
why: Equal coefficients ({k}) on x² and y², and no xy term: a circle.
Different coefficients on x² and y² give an ellipse.
Opposite signs on x² and y² give a hyperbola.
Only x is squared: that is a parabola.

working: |z − p| = k|z − q| → square → x² and y² have equal coefficients → circle (k ≠ 1)
k = 1 → the squares cancel → a straight line

exercises.q: Find the radius of the circle x² + y² {-2*a|s}x {-2*b|s}y {a*a+b*b-r*r|s} = 0.
|z − {p}| = {k}|z| describes a circle. Find its centre as p + qi. Enter p and q.
exercises.ex: Square both sides: (x − {p})² + y² = {k*k}(x² + y²), which gives centre ({-u}, 0).
